scope: National household debt, loan rates, federal and state/local government debt, student-loan law after Pub. L. 119-21, bankruptcy basics and credit-score calibration; per-place payday status, small-loan cap class, general usury cap and state+local debt per resident. An unread field is null with its evidence status, never zero. Real data calibrates only.

other.question: New York Fed Q2 2026 'other' (consumer finance, retail) balance; not in snippets. Do not derive as a residual: the other totals are rounded.

student90PlusShareOfBalance.note: Seriously delinquent (90+ days) share; exact New York Fed measure (stock share vs. transition rate) not confirmed

auto90Plus.note: Measure (stock share vs. annualized transition rate) not confirmed

creditCard90Plus.question: New York Fed Q2 2026 credit card 90+ day delinquency (stock and transition rate)

mortgage90Plus.question: New York Fed Q2 2026 mortgage 90+ day delinquency

heloc90Plus.question: New York Fed Q2 2026 HELOC 90+ day delinquency

other90Plus.question: New York Fed Q2 2026 'other' 90+ day delinquency

byBorrowerAge.question: New York Fed Q2 2026 debt balance by borrower age group (18-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+) and transitions by age; report PDF unreachable

scf2022.note: Survey of Consumer Finances 2022, families (not individuals). Medians are among families holding that debt, 2022 dollars.

shareWithCreditCardBalance.note: about 45 percent; carrying a balance after last payment

shareWithAnyDebt.question: SCF 2022 share of families with any debt and median total debt

vehicleLoans.question: SCF 2022 share holding vehicle installment loans and median balance

byAgeOfHead.question: SCF 2022 holding shares and medians by age of head (<35, 35-44, 45-54, 55-64, 65-74, 75+); SCF table tool unreachable

paydayTypicalAPR.note: CFPB: a two-week loan at $15 per $100 equates to 'almost 400 percent' APR; 391 is the arithmetic (15/100 x 365/14 = 391.07), not a CFPB-published figure

militaryLendingActMAPRCap.note: Covers active-duty service members and dependents; MAPR includes most fees, credit insurance and add-on products; state law cannot raise it

payment.value: 1 to 10 percent of adjusted gross income per year, minus $50 per month per dependent, minimum $10 per month

unpaidInterest.value: Interest not covered by the payment is waived; if principal falls less than $50 in a month, the government makes up the difference

repaymentAssistancePlan.newLoansOnOrAfter2026-07-01: Only a standard plan or RAP; IBR, PAYE and SAVE are closed to new loans (snippet-derived, secondary)

legacyPlans.value: SAVE, PAYE and ICR borrowers must move to an eligible plan by July 1, 2028

undergraduateLimits.question: Confirm undergraduate annual/aggregate Direct Loan limits unchanged by Pub. L. 119-21 (statute text on Congress.gov not reachable)

ibrForExistingBorrowers.question: Exact IBR changes for existing borrowers (e.g., removal of partial-financial-hardship test) and dates; confirm from statute text

statutoryDebtLimit.note: Raised by $5.0 trillion on 2025-07-04 by Pub. L. 119-21; had been reinstated at $36.1 trillion on 2025-01-02

netInterestFY2025.question: Exact FY2025 net interest outlays in dollars; CBO snippet says only that it surpassed $1 trillion for the first time

stateCreditRatings.note: Calibration only. Snippet-derived; agency and date often unspecified. Verify with S&P's 'U.S. State Ratings And Outlooks: Current List' before use.

aaaStatesAgencyUnspecified.note: Snippet described these as AAA per 2025 data without naming the agency; list is not exhaustive

US-IL.question: Illinois S&P and Moody's ratings as of 2026; snippet said 'BBB as of 2025' without agency, which conflicts with other reports of upgrades

US-CA.question: California ratings as of 2026; snippet 'AA-' (2024-25) without agency

US-NJ.question: New Jersey ratings as of 2026; snippet 'A-' (2024) without agency

US-KY.question: Kentucky ratings as of 2026; snippet 'A+' without agency

censusLongTermDebtOutstanding.question: Census ALFIN (latest year, likely FY2023) total long-term debt outstanding, state vs. local, national and by state; census.gov unreachable from this session

reasonAcfrBased2023.note: Different concept from Census debt outstanding: includes pension and retiree-health liabilities. Do not use as Census bonded debt.

goVersusRevenueShare.question: National share of state and local bonded debt that is general obligation vs. revenue bonds (e.g., Census ALFIN 'full faith and credit' vs. 'nonguaranteed' split)

US-CA.detail: 92N: state GO needs voter majority (art. XVI, sec. 1). Confirmed: debt over $300,000 needs two-thirds of each house and a majority of voters.

US-NY.detail: 92N: state GO needs voter referendum (art. VII, sec. 11). Confirmed: majority at a general election.

US-FL.detail: 92N: state GO needs voter approval. Confirmed: full-faith-and-credit bonds need a vote of the electors.

US-TX.detail: 92N: state GO needs a constitutional amendment. Confirmed: voters must approve a constitutional amendment authorizing GO debt.

US-WA.detail: 92N: no voter approval, debt service capped at 9 percent of general state revenues. Voter-approval value agrees; the cap is out of date: the 2012 amendment set 8.25 percent from July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2034 (8.0 percent after), on a six-year revenue average including state property tax. Flag for correction.

chapter7.value: Liquidation: a trustee sells nonexempt assets and pays creditors; no repayment plan

chapter13.value: Repayment plan of three years if current monthly income is below the state median, generally five years if above

meansTest.value: Income test for Chapter 7 against the state median; failing it generally routes the filer to Chapter 13

creditReportYears.note: CFPB: up to 10 years from the order for relief or adjudication. This corpus does not use the common 7-year credit-bureau practice for completed Chapter 13 because the cited snippet does not establish it.

chapter13SevenYearPractice.question: Official or bureau source for removing completed Chapter 13 after 7 years

annualFilings.question: U.S. Courts bankruptcy filings, 12 months ending June 30, 2026, by chapter

averageFICO.note: FICO reported the average dipping to 714 in 2025

bandShares.note: Figures came from a search summary that did not name the originating publisher reliably; they sum to 100 percent. Treat as low-confidence until confirmed from FICO or Experian.
